:::{#def-ball}
#### Open and closed balls

Let $\vx \in \reals^p$ and $r > 0$.
The **open ball** of radius $r$ around $\vx$ is the set
$\cb{\vy \in \reals^p : \norm{\vy - \vx} < r}$,
of points whose distance from $\vx$
(the [Euclidean norm](linear-algebra.qmd#def-euclidean-norm) of the difference)
is less than $r$.
The **closed ball** of radius $r$ around $\vx$ is
$\cb{\vy \in \reals^p : \norm{\vy - \vx} \le r}$.
The open and closed balls of radius $1$ around $\vzero$
are the open and closed **unit balls**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-ball}
#### Points in the unit balls of $\reals^2$

- $\tp{(0.5, 0.5)}$ has

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \norm{\tp{(0.5, 0.5)}}^2 &= 0.25 + 0.25 \\
  &= 0.5 \\
  &< 1,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  so it is in both the open and the closed unit ball.
- $\tp{(0.6, 0.8)}$ has

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \norm{\tp{(0.6, 0.8)}}^2 &= 0.36 + 0.64 \\
  &= 1,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  so it is in the closed unit ball but not the open one.
- For $p = 1$, the open ball of radius $r$ around $c$ is the open interval $(c - r, c + r)$.

:::
